text:
Alex P.: quick sync — proposing a 'slimline' installer network surface for on-prem customers. goal: reduce ops friction for small netops teams while keeping rollback and observability guarantees. thoughts? :wave:
Mira (Field): love the idea. main asks from customers: no inbound ports, predictable egress, clear rollback lanes. acme wants an installer that can run behind strict egress proxies.
Jonah (NetOps): +1. for predictable egress we need egress-ip pinning and an option to announce a static NAT. also need docs for DNAT/port mapping customers.
Claire (Eng): technical constraints: operator-relay currently opens 6443 inbound for kube controlplane. we can flip to agent-initiated websocket tunnel to avoid inbound. trade is a little more latency during staging probes.
Mira (Field): can we make that agent-initiated behavior the default for the slimline profile? field teams prefer opt-out rather than opt-in.
Claire (Eng): yes, we can. plan: add --mode=outbound-proxy to installer profile. minimal code snippet we plan to ship in v0.8:
```
installer:
  profile: slimline
  network:
    mode: outbound-proxy
    egress_pin: true
    relay_port: 443
```
Jonah (NetOps): looks good. need acceptance criteria: 1) no inbound ports required for controlplane after install, 2) egress IP stable for 72h under churn tests, 3) canary upgrade revert < 15 minutes, 4) audit logs show handoffs with KMS key id.
Alex P.: adding that to the launch checklist. also propose that rollback must support both operator-shim and full uninstall+reinstall paths (customer choice).
Mira (Field): field ask: provide a migration path from existing installs that currently use inbound ports. we need an automated conversion that preserves tenant IPs if possible.
Claire (Eng): migration sketch: step 1) deploy agent-outbound alongside existing operator; step 2) sync KV cache and test tunnels; step 3) flip traffic. We'll build a dry-run mode that reports delta.
Jonah (NetOps): one more netops constraint: for customers behind strict proxies we need a documented list of TLS SNI and ALPN values and healthcheck endpoints. also add a fallback to TCP-level relay if websocket is blocked.
Alex P.: good call. I'll add SNI/ALPN table to the docs and a troubleshooting section.
Mira (Field): can we expose a one-click support dump to capture egress IP, tunnel status, and recent upgrade steps? support teams want that to reduce back-and-forth.
Claire (Eng): yes, we'll add `redwoodctl support-bundle --slimline` that includes:
- egress_ip.txt
- relay_connection.log
- upgrade_trace.json
- installer-config.yaml
Jonah (NetOps): for launch gating we should require two pilot customers (one behind corporate proxy, one airgapped via relay appliance) pass end-to-end.
Alex P.: agreed. timeline proposal: prototype this week, internal dogfood next week, pilot signoff in 3 weeks. launch gating: pilots green, acceptance tests pass, docs + support bundle live.
deploy-bot: deploy status: infra/slimline-net-profile prototype deployed to staging at 2024-11-02T09:12:07Z :white_check_mark:
Mira (Field): awesome. will coordinate pilot invites. final ask: include clear rollback messaging for customers that cannot tolerate any tenant IP change. we may need to offer a pin-preserve migration flag.
Claire (Eng): we'll add `--preserve-tenant-ips` to migration dry-run and document limitations.
Alex P.: thanks all — I'll capture checklist and follow up with sprint card. tagging @jonah for netops signoff when tests are in. :thumbsup:
